title: The Blank page in the book
subtitle: 文学写作 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）
meta: 主题语境：文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）　|　核心词汇：blank　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 blank 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the fisherman wrote of ① a blank page in the book in the logbook, and everybody in the harbour said at once that it was ② blanker than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the fisherman, who never explained anything, had done it with great care and gone home; it was the blank ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the blankest page in the book anybody in the harbour had ever seen, or so the logbook for July 1954 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too blank to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the boatman who had come to help; the blank ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the net at the far pier, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a blank look on his face, and said that no boatman in his right mind would call it ⑥ as blank as the look on his face they had once had in the old harbour. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was blank or not, and he said so.

By 1967 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the logbook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something blank, and nothing besides. The boatman from the next harbour called the whole plan ⑧ quite blank; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the logbook kept the names of the blank ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1970, on the same day, she wrote of another blank page in the book in the same logbook, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ blanker than anybody had expected. ⑩ The blankest look on his face in the whole harbour, she said in 1972, was the one she could never quite name; the blank ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 空白（前置定语 a blank page in the book：1960 年渔人在航海日志里记下的那件空白的空页）
B. adj. 空白／茫然（比较级 blanker than：文中两处，一处比书里的空页，一处比预想）
C. adj. 空白／茫然（最高级 the blankest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 空白（表语 too blank to do：母亲觉得它太空白，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 茫然（前置定语 a blank look on his face：叔叔把整件事称作一桩茫然的神情）
F. adj. 茫然（同级比较 as blank as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩脸上茫然的神情相比）
G. adj. 茫然（后置定语 something blank：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 茫然（受程度副词修饰 quite blank：那位船工的评价）

items.q: a blank page in the book
the blankest page in the book anybody
a blank look on his face
The blankest look on his face in

answers.why: blank 意为“空白”，1960 年渔人在航海日志里记下的是“一件空白的空页”，此处作前置定语 a blank page in the book。
blank 意为“空白”，此处用比较级 blanker than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
blank 意为“空白”，航海日志上 七月 那行字说它是渔港里最空白的一件，故用最高级 the blankest page in the book。
blank 意为“空白”，母亲认为这件东西“太空白了，谁也用不上”，too blank to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
blank 意为“茫然”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩茫然的神情”，此处作前置定语 a blank look on his face。
blank 意为“茫然”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩脸上茫然的神情一样茫然”，同级比较用 as blank as。
blank 意为“茫然”，航海日志上那半行字要的是“茫然的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something blank。
blank 意为“茫然”，邻渔港来的那位船工认为这套计划“相当茫然”，quite 修饰原级 blank。
blank 意为“茫然”，1970 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要茫然”，故用比较级 blanker than。
blank 意为“茫然”，母亲 1972 年说的是“整个渔港里最茫然的那一桩”，故用最高级 the blankest look on his face。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1960 年，渔人在航海日志里记下了一件空白的空页。（a blank page in the book）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更空白。（blanker than …）
母亲觉得它太空白，谁也用不上。（too blank to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩茫然的神情。（a blank look on his face）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩脸上茫然的神情一样茫然。（as blank as …）
到了 1967 年，航海日志上只剩半行字：要的是一件茫然的东西。（something blank）
answers: In 1960 the fisherman wrote of a blank page in the book in the logbook.
Everybody said it was blanker than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too blank to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a blank look on his face.
He said nobody would call it as blank as the look on his face they had once had.
By 1967 the logbook asked for nothing but something blank.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 blank 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1960 the fisherman wrote of a blank page in the book in the logbook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the blankest page in the book in the harbour, or so the logbook says.
My mother thought it too blank to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a blank look on his face, and nobody argued with him.
The boatman from the next harbour called the plan quite blank, and everybody laughed.
The blank ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
